_comment: wh_chain30_solve_500 with an explicit SPATIAL PARTITION of the deployed chain over the K1's eight harts: yolo on the four P cores, nav on CPU_E#0, control on CPU_E#1, one hart per dispatch (shard_only_networks: none). Everything else -- windows, periods, instance counts, horizon, chain deadline -- is identical to wh_chain30_solve_500, so the two solves differ only in placement freedom. The P-core pin is an instruction-set fact, not a preference: smt.vmadot (IME) is legal only on cluster 0, probed per hart in ModelBlaster/artifacts/ime_isa_probe/FINDINGS.md, so this is the placement under which the whole of yolo is IME-eligible. nav and control get a hart each so neither shares a core with perception. Widening is off because four harts cannot both carry a wide yolo block and pipeline frames: a 4-hart block occupies the whole cluster for its duration, so no two frames overlap -- see docs/partitioned_schedule.md for the measured cost.

chain.deadline_rationale: a frame's goal reaches control within its nav window (77.8 ms); control is phase-locked at 100 Hz and acts on the newest goal
